findings.title: Wrong ESM detection
findings.body:
`referencedModuleKind >= ModuleKind.ES2015` also matches `Node16` (100), `NodeNext` (199) and `Preserve` (200). Under those modes, a file's real format depends on its own `impliedNodeFormat` (package.json `type`, `.cts`/`.mts`), not on the project setting.

Example: a referenced project with `module: nodenext` that emits CommonJS. Its declarations are treated as ESM and lose the synthetic default, so consumers get false TS1192 errors.

Separately, `?? ModuleKind.CommonJS` ignores how the module kind defaults from `target`. With `target: es2015+` and no `module`, the emit is ES2015, but this code treats it as CommonJS. Use `getEmitModuleKind(referencedOptions)` and the file's implied node format instead.

findings.title: Wrong option consulted
findings.body:
`allowSyntheticDefaultImports` is a type-checking setting for the importing project. It says nothing about the referenced project's emitted JS.

Example: a referenced CommonJS library without `esModuleInterop` has this flag false. Any consumer that does enable synthetic defaults now gets "has no default export" when it default-imports that library. Previously this was allowed, and at runtime the import works via the consumer's interop.

This check should be removed. The importing program's own `allowSyntheticDefaultImports`, which is already checked earlier in this function, is the right gate.

findings.title: Baseline regression
findings.body:
This existing test, `default-import-interop-uses-referenced-project-settings`, now gains two new TS1192 errors for default imports from `lib/dist/a`.

The test name suggests these imports were meant to be allowed based on the referenced project's settings. The new errors look like a behavioral regression caused by the checks above, not an intended baseline update. Please verify the referenced project's options in this test and confirm whether these errors are expected.
